merges.sentence: Students may use AI only when the instructor or assignment explicitly permits it.
merges.why: All make AI use conditional on explicit instructor or assignment permission.

merges.sentence: Using AI against the course AI policy is an academic integrity violation.
merges.why: Both classify policy-breaking AI use as academic dishonesty.

merges.sentence: Students must disclose or cite any AI use in their work, including permitted use.
merges.why: All require acknowledging every AI use; undisclosed use is the violation.

merges.sentence: Students must cite all sources and outside help, including AI, as they would any source.
merges.why: Both require citing AI like any other source.

merges.sentence: Students must not ask AI to produce answers, solutions or code for graded assignments.
merges.why: All forbid having AI generate the assignment's solution.

merges.sentence: Students must not submit AI-generated code or text as their own work.
merges.why: All forbid putting AI output into a submission as one's own.

merges.sentence: Students must produce the work they submit themselves.
merges.why: Both state the submitted work must be the student's own production.

merges.sentence: Students may draw on AI code examples but must rewrite rather than copy them.
merges.why: Both forbid direct copying of AI code and require the student's own version.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI to debug or fix their own code.
merges.why: Both prohibit AI debugging of the student's code.

merges.sentence: Students may ask AI to explain course concepts and material.
merges.why: Both permit conceptual questions to AI about course material.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI to support their learning and understanding.
merges.why: Both permit AI as a learning aid.

merges.sentence: Students should use AI to support their learning, never to replace it.
merges.why: All forbid AI use that substitutes for the student's learning.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI in place of their own thinking and work.
merges.why: All forbid outsourcing the student's own thinking or work to AI.

merges.sentence: Students must understand and be able to explain all code they submit.
merges.why: All require comprehension of every submitted line, including AI code.

merges.sentence: Students are accountable for all content they submit, including AI-generated content.
merges.why: Both place responsibility for submitted AI content on the student.

merges.sentence: Students must verify and critically evaluate AI output before using it.
merges.why: Both require checking AI output rather than accepting it.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI coding assistants or autocomplete such as Copilot.
merges.why: All ban in-editor AI code assistants.

merges.sentence: Students must interact with AI only through a chat interface.
merges.why: Both restrict AI to chat rather than agents or editor tools.

merges.sentence: Students should ask staff when unsure whether an AI use or tool is allowed.
merges.why: Both ask students to consult staff under uncertainty about AI use.

merges.sentence: Students should seek help from course staff rather than from AI.
merges.why: Both direct students to human staff over AI for help.

merges.sentence: Using AI is optional, and students may opt out.
merges.why: Both state AI use is not required.

merges.sentence: Students are not required to pay for AI tools.
merges.why: Both state no purchase is needed.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI, but are discouraged from it.
merges.why: Both state AI is permitted but discouraged.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI as a consultant or limited helper, not as an author.
merges.why: Both permit AI only in a helper role.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI, which counts as forbidden outside help.
merges.why: Both ban AI as unauthorized outside help or sources.

merges.sentence: Students must write their own tests and not have AI generate test cases.
merges.why: Both forbid outsourcing test cases to AI.

merges.sentence: Students must not use any AI tool other than the course's approved one.
merges.why: Both restrict AI to the course tool.

merges.sentence: Students must use AI responsibly and within the stated limits and policies.
merges.why: Both require responsible, policy-compliant AI use.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI for exam study, self-testing and practice problems.
merges.why: Both permit AI for self-testing practice.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI in class or discussions unless the instructor permits.
merges.why: Both ban in-class AI use absent permission.

merges.sentence: Students must avoid AI interactions that produce solution code.
merges.why: Both require steering AI away from generating code.

merges.sentence: Students are invited to share their AI experiences and feedback.
merges.why: Both invite optional sharing of AI use experiences.
